newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates coast at highs.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates coast at highs.

text.p: Overnight guilders stayed pinned to pre-weekend highs on Monday with little prospect of falling substantially in the immediate future, dealers said.
Call money was quoted at 2.81 to 2.93 percent bid, with the majority of deals being done at 2.87 percent. This compared with a bid rate of 2.81 percent on Friday.
Dealers said that as a result of the high call rates some bidders were switching to one-week deposits, which were quoting around 2.84/2.93 percent bid/offer.
"Several market players had been expecting an influx of government payments which didn't materialise," one said.
Another said the finance ministry's programmes of Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) were underpinning prices.

"As long as the government is still looking for money under these programmes call money rates are unlikely to come down substantially -- unless it nets so much cash it can afford to offer less attractive rates," he said.
But dealers said lastingly high call rates were unlikely to lead to a hike in the rate on special advances, currently pegged at 2.50 percent.
"I don't see it happening," said one, adding call rates had risen on the back of the current liquidity shortage.
He said the Dutch central bank was not likely to be keeping liquidity purposely tight with a view to hiking the special advances rate.
"It's more a case of the market's needs being difficult to gauge right now," he said.

Dealers said most activity was limited to deposits of up to one month. One-month deposits were well-bid at 2.96 percent bid from 2.90 percent on Friday, driven up by end-of-year window dressing but with few offers.
